# Measured Vocabulary — the words Dan actually uses

**This page is generated. Do not hand-edit it** — run `bin/wiki-lexicon mine` then `bin/wiki-lexicon page`. It states no finding: it is the arithmetic, and a conclusion drawn from it reaches an ordinary page through the normal operations.

Every other lexicon in this wiki records words somebody *chose* — the 200 curated terms on [[wiki/interests/language/vocabulary-lexicon]], the ~25 recalled coinages on [[wiki/interests/language/personal-lexicon]]. This one records words somebody *counted*, against a contrast corpus, so that "distinctive" means something a reader can check.

## Coverage

| | |
|---|---|
| Messages Dan sent | 131,196 |
| Messages Dan received (the contrast corpus) | 130,402 |
| Dan's texting tokens | 1,334,932 |
| Their tokens | 1,063,405 |
| Dan's AI-prompt turns (ChatGPT export, 2022–2025) | 1,456 |
| Dan's AI-prompt tokens | 93,798 |

Rows by export, after deduplication on (date, time, direction, text): **csv** 55,194, **dump** 206,404. Neither export covers the record alone — the dump stops in 2025 and the CSV is thin on 2024 — so both are read and the union is what is counted.

## What marks his speech

Log-odds ratio with an informative Dirichlet prior, Dan's sent text against everything he received. The score is a z-statistic, so a rare word cannot outrank a common one on ratio alone. Counts are raw occurrences.

**The Gemini column is not clean and cannot be made clean.** His Gemini prompts average ~1,186 characters against ChatGPT's ~422 because he pastes documents into them; a ranked word list over that corpus returns `div`, `class`, `null` and `data-v-` at the top. An exact match on a multi-word term is immune to that and a frequency ranking is not, which is why this tool computes the first and refuses the second.
